title: Example 13-4: Poem with Deep Indention

illustrates.quote: Use normal poetry indention when print is deeply indented.

blocks.features: Untitled excerpt (from a translation of Homer's Iliad); print deeply indents the 3rd line ("So he shouted") far to the right, well beyond an ordinary sub-entry indent -- the very deep print indention this example's title refers to.

lines.text: if the best of immortals really drives me on,
Hera’s lord whose thunder drums the sky!”
Lashing the rage and fighting-fury in every Trojan.

print.notes: Picture on PDF p.358; "So he shouted" is printed far to the right of the print column (well past a normal sub-entry tab stop), illustrating the deep print indention that rule 13.3.1.d says braille should NOT reproduce literally.

braille.notes: Verbatim from .txt lines 10330-10334, after stripping a 9-space fixed left margin shared by every line of this boxed example (measured as the minimum leading-space run; plain ASCII padding, not braille content). Line 1 is a fully blank 40-cell braille line (all-blank cells, U+2800×40 before conversion) -- a genuine blank line, not decoration; consistent with 13.3.1.a's 'leave a blank line before...a poem'. Per rule 13.3.1.d, the deeply-indented print line 'So he shouted' is NOT given deep braille indention: it instead gets only a normal 2-cell (cell-3) runover indent, i.e. it is treated as a continuation/runover of the previous poetic line rather than a new, deeply indented one.

uncertain: The print poem's source/author is not named in this inline example; identified only as a Homer/Iliad-style translation excerpt from its content and register, not confirmed against a citation in the source.
resolution: braille.lines identical between runs except index 0: both runs agree the source shows a full 40-cell blank braille row at this position (.txt line 10330, confirmed: 40 literal U+2800 characters after the 9-space box margin -- a genuine content row, part of the excerpt, not page filler), but run A rendered it as 40 literal ASCII spaces while run B rendered it as "". Resolved in favour of run B's "": every other blank line in the entire existing gold corpus (304 instances checked across sections 1/4/7/8/9/11/16 and UKAAF appendix-e/g) is represented as "", never as a non-empty string of spaces -- run A's own stated method ("trailing spaces stripped") already implies "" here too; keeping the padded form would be the only non-"" blank line in the whole repository's gold data for no evidenced reason. Run A and run B independently transcribed this item's braille.lines identically, character-for-character; independently re-verified against the cited source .txt lines (U+2800 blank cells / ASCII-space converted, reference-line-number or box-margin field measured and stripped per this section's own convention) as part of this reconciliation. print.blocks content agreed in substance between both runs (only prose-wording differences in `features`/`notes`, not resolved as errors); run A's wording is kept. See compare-gold-13/differences.md for the file-by-file account. CORRECTION during buildModel13 integration: print.blocks poem line 'So he shouted' had indent:3 (run A) vs indent:1 (run B) -- an A/B disagreement not caught by the braille.lines-only diff. Resolved in favour of run B (1): the gold braille (.txt line 10333) measures exactly 2 leading blank cells for this line -- nestedMargins's first=level*2 gives 2 only for level 1, not level 3 (which would be 6). Rule 13.3.1d itself confirms this reading: 'Use NORMAL poetry indention when print is deeply indented' -- the deep PRINT indentation this example's title refers to is deliberately normalized down to one ordinary sub-level (cell 3) in braille, not reproduced at its own visual depth.
